clue.text: Absent players chucked out

parts.note: the players in a production are its cast
someone absent is away

explanation.surface: A team's missing players have been thrown out of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absent players' reads as a phrase about a team, but the two words supply the pieces in the opposite order to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cast away has been discarded or thrown out, the sense of a marooned sailor too.

clue.text: Carefully inspect patient

definitions.meaning: to ... a place is to look it over carefully, as a burglar does
a doctor speaks of a patient as a ...

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to examine a patient thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to reconnoitre a place, and a medical case meaning a person treated.

clue.text: Bear of suspicious nature disheartened, showing unsociability

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it
taken as written

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the nine-letter word goes

parts.note: fishiness is a dubious, suspicious quality

explanation.surface: A bear with a shifty character is sulking and avoiding company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the central I of FISHINESS, leaving FISHNESS; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aloof and cold towards others is a direct synonym for unsociability.

clue.text: Religious rite in the form of cleansings, say

indicators.note: say tells us the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: in the form of means as, and cleansings are purges

explanation.surface: A church ceremony described as a sort of ritual washing.
explanation.walkthrough: AS PURGES spoken sounds like the Latin name of the rite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asperges is the Catholic ceremony of sprinkling the congregation with holy water before Mass.

clue.text: Person not fit for children to see

definitions.meaning: a grown-up person, as opposed to a child

definitions.text: not fit for children to see
definitions.meaning: films and material labelled for grown-ups only are restricted from children

explanation.surface: Someone whom youngsters should not be allowed to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a grown person and an adjective for content restricted to grown-ups.

clue.text: Holder, for example, wants good trophy

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A sports club's captain, say, wants a decent trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holder' looks like a title-holder in a sporting picture; it is the definition, an object that holds something. 'wants' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holds a boiled egg at the breakfast table, so it is a holder.

clue.text: Dark blue

explanation.surface: A deep shade of the colour blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both poorly lit and despondent, matching each definition.

clue.text: Drunk, and what did you say? Plenty!

parts.note: cut is British slang for tipsy
taken as written
come again? is a request to repeat what was said

explanation.surface: A tipsy person mishears and asks for a repeat, then shouts that there's lots.
explanation.walkthrough: CUT meaning drunk is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-and-come-again is a plentiful supply, like a joint one can keep slicing from.

clue.text: Longs to dress a fool in baggy trousers

indicators.note: to dress here means to clothe, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
taken as written
a loon is a silly person

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to clothe a clown in voluminous trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longs' looks like a noun for trousers, but it is the verb meaning yearns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantaloons are loose wide trousers, originally those of the Pantaloon character in comedy.

clue.text: Bodoni's sort, on the surface

definitions.note: read as Bodoni is, a noun phrase naming an example

parts.note: a sort or kind is a type
the face of something is its surface

explanation.surface: A description of the sort of thing Bodoni was, at least superficially.
explanation.walkthrough: Bodoni is a classic printing type designed by Giambattista Bodoni; 'Bodoni's' reads as 'Bodoni is'. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodoni is a well-known example of a printing font design.

clue.text: Tax paid on legal documents to impress office

parts.note: to impress a mark is to stamp it
an office in the sense of a duty or function

explanation.surface: A levy on legal papers that's meant to make the bureaucracy look impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp duty is the British tax levied on documents such as property transfers.

clue.text: Frequently put in a softener

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the next word

explanation.surface: Advice to add something to fabric conditioner regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something many times is a direct synonym for doing it frequently.

clue.text: Smell reported in European river

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so we want a word heard alike

parts.note: a smell is an odour

explanation.surface: A bad smell is noticed in a river on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder flows through Czechia and along the Polish-German border to the Baltic.

clue.text: The foreign land, one with a religious delusion

parts.note: taken as written
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone from a distant country with a fanatical belief that they are divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Theomania is the delusion of believing oneself to be a god, so a religious mania.

clue.text: Get rid of gold, for instance — it's going to be melted down

definitions.text: it's going to be melted down

parts.note: to scrap is to discard
gold is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: Disposing of gold jewellery that will end up in a furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal goods are collected for recycling by being melted into fresh stock.

clue.text: In cafe, no beef, unfortunately: this, though?

definitions.text: In cafe, no beef, unfortunately: this, though?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A café with no beef on the menu still has something on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a café without beef will still have this. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole clue: what a café without meat would still certainly stock, the roasted seed for drinks.

clue.text: Soundly criticise wood in fashionable little shop

indicators.note: soundly tells us the words are to be heard

parts.note: to criticise is to boo, and teak is a wood

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly rubbishes the timber fittings in a trendy shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' qualifying 'criticise'; it is the homophone signal. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small shop selling stylish clothes or accessories.

clue.text: Satellite repeater

definitions.meaning: a reflected sound that repeats what was said

explanation.surface: A satellite that relays signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo 1 was a 1960 balloon satellite, and a reverberation repeats a sound.

clue.text: A shaped block — of sandalwood?

parts.note: playfully reads sandalwood as wood for a sandal: a foot-shaped block kept inside footwear

explanation.surface: A carved piece of fragrant wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandalwood is a fragrant timber, but here it is split into a sandal (footwear) and wood (a tree).
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-shaped device inserted into footwear to keep its form is made of wood.

clue.text: Greedy boy losing his head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: David is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A gluttonous lad is about to lose his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager and craving, a close synonym of greedy.

clue.text: Divine stewed prunes, with hesitant expression, are swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed means taken in, so one part goes inside the other
stewed fruit is cooked down and mixed, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: hum is the sound of someone hesitating, as in hum and haw
A is the abbreviation of are, the metric unit of area

explanation.surface: Someone declares stewed prunes heavenly, hesitantly, as they gulp them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' scrambles PRUNES into SUPERN, which takes in HUM and A. 'Divine' looks like an adjective of praise for the dish; it is the definition. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine beings have powers above those of humans, so divine is close to superhuman.

clue.text: Jewish ascetic, not cold in heart

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the heart of a matter is its essence
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Jewish holy man who is anything but cold-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period.

clue.text: Support that helps artist match silk for reproduction

indicators.note: reproduction suggests a copy made anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An artist's helper is matching a piece of silk to copy it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahlstick is a padded rod a painter rests the brush hand on for steadiness.

clue.text: Use hawser to haul ketch initially over ridge

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second
initially means we want just the first letter of the word

parts.note: a ridge is an edge, as of a hill

explanation.surface: A sailor pulls a small sailing boat across a ridge with a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: A ketch is a two-masted boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To kedge is to move a ship by hauling on a rope attached to a dropped anchor.

clue.text: Dairy product created the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means read backwards

parts.note: something created is made

explanation.surface: A dairy item produced by an incorrect method.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese, an example of a dairy product.

clue.text: Date that is timeless

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A date that will never expire.
explanation.walkthrough: The ides was a fixed day in the Roman calendar, such as 15 March.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the ides was a set day each month, so a date.

clue.text: Note about fringe subject

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a hem is the edge or fringe of a garment

explanation.surface: A memo concerning a matter on the edge of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme of a talk or essay is its subject.

clue.text: Junior worker is sneaky

parts.note: a junior is lower in rank, so under
a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: A junior employee is underhand in their dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealings are secret and dishonest, so sneaky.

clue.text: Once liked to be inclined from the vertical

definitions.meaning: an archaic verb list meant to please or wish, so once liked
a ship that heels over to one side leans away from upright

explanation.surface: Someone who used to enjoy leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic list means to choose or like; a ship that lists leans to one side.

clue.text: For the auditor, degrades landed properties

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is to be heard

parts.note: to degrade someone is to demean them

explanation.surface: A listener is told that someone belittles the owners of country estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the auditor' looks like an accountant, but an auditor is literally a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is an estate held by a lord, land in his own possession.
